name: French Third Republic

areaKm2.note: world_1914 France polygon = ~530,000 km2 computed on the sphere; published metropolitan area 536,464 km2 (B&H Table 1: 0.5M km2).

population.note: Broadberry and Harrison 2005 Table 1: France 1913 = 39.8M (League of Nations 1927); B&H Table 9 (Urlanis) 39.6M; OWID/HYDE 1914 = 39.58M (low). COW tpop 1914 = 33.2M reflects the occupied departments and is not used. Metropolitan France only; colonies (48.3M) excluded.

urbanization.note: HYDE (OWID) urban share France 1910 = 47.5%. 1911 census: 44% urban (communes of 2,000+ agglomerated). Low ~38% in towns of 5,000+.

activePersonnel.note: Cited page: mobilisation ordered 1 Aug 1914 called the classes of 1896-1910, almost three million reservists, on top of the ~0.8M serving conscripts (three-year law); Mid = ~0.8M + ~3M from the cited page, rounded down for exemptions; bounds are a judgement band. Field armies of the north-east ~1.65M in 62 infantry divisions (British Army page). Navy ~60,000 included. Snapshot month: August 1914. Check: COW NMC v7 milper 1914 = 789k, 1915 = 4,997k (annual averages, not the snapshot-date strength).

trainedReserves.note: Older territorial reserve classes (ages 42-48, Reserve of the Territorial Army) not yet called in August, plus colonial reservists. France trained ~85% of each class, so almost every adult man had service. Reconstruction, grade C.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Doughty, Pyrrhic Victory (isbn:0-674-01880-X), not read from a fetched source. Artillery (87 regiments, 40% of the army by 1918), engineers, trains, depots of 201 reserve and 145 territorial regiments in training, staffs, navy.

mobilizationRatio.note: Total mobilised: 7,935,000 (French reply to the ILO, 1924) or 8,410,000 (US War Dept) on the cited page, incl. ~0.5-0.9M colonial troops; metropolitan ~7.9M / 39.7M = 0.20.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Cited page: 1.5 million infantry in 1915 (850,000 in 1918). August 1914: 47 active and 25 reserve infantry divisions plus territorial divisions and regiments.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Lebel 1886 rifle, few MGs (St Etienne unreliable), red trousers, no steel helmet until 1915

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: three-year conscripts; offensive a outrance doctrine cost 300,000 casualties by mid-September

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Doughty, Pyrrhic Victory (isbn:0-674-01880-X), not read from a fetched source. 31 active battalions of chasseurs a pied/alpins plus their reserve battalions (~1,700 each).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: same weapons, mountain equipment

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75-1.0. Evidence: elite chasseurs alpins

count.note: 79 cavalry regiments on the cited page (~700 sabres each), 10 cavalry divisions plus divisional squadrons; cuirassiers rode with the light cavalry in the screening role.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: carbine and sabre/lance, cuirasses; horses broke down in August

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: regular cavalry

count.note: Cited page: 4,986 75 mm Mle 1897 (3,680 with the field corps), 128 65 mm mountain guns, 210 120 mm C 1890 and 104 155 mm Rimailho howitzers, plus a few hundred heavy pieces drawn from fortresses.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: the 75 the best field gun of 1914 (12-18 rounds/min), but almost no modern heavy artillery

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: excellent direct-fire gunnery

count.note: Cited page: France had 156 aeroplanes at the outbreak (against Russia's 263); the Aviation in WWI page gives ~184 Allied aircraft in the west incl. ~30 British. Unarmed reconnaissance types; no fighters existed. Airships excluded.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: Bleriot, Farman, Caudron, Voisin; French engine industry the best in 1914

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: 1911-13 exercises pioneered artillery spotting (Aviation in WWI page)

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. Conway's 1906-1921: 2 Courbet dreadnoughts in service (France and Paris commissioned Aug-Oct 1914), 6 Danton semi-dreadnoughts, ~13 older pre-dreadnoughts, ~19 armoured and ~8 protected cruisers. Most of the fleet in the Mediterranean (Halpern ch. 1).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: mixed pre-dreadnought fleet, few dreadnoughts

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: long-service crews, weak fleet tactics

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. ~84 torpilleurs d'escadre (destroyers); 135 smaller torpedo boats excluded.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: small 300-800 t destroyers

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Mediterranean blockade duty

count.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. ~67 submarines in service, many small early boats (Conway's).

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: many steam or petrol boats

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: pioneer submarine service

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.5-0.75. Evidence: Joffre's Plan XVII failed in the Battle of the Frontiers, but the general staff re-deployed by rail and won the Marne; ~40% of generals sacked by year end

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.75. Evidence: regionally recruited conscript army that held after losing 260,000 men in August-September

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.75-1.0 (motivated, defence of the homeland). Evidence: Union sacree; invaded homeland, recovery of Alsace-Lorraine

weapons.note: Anchor: 7 (1905). Evidence: 75 mm Mle 1897 QF gun, Lebel rifle; few heavy howitzers and MGs

armor.note: Anchor: 7 (armoured cars, steel helmet 1915). Evidence: no helmets (Adrian from Sep 1915, cited page); a few armoured cars

ships.note: Anchor: 7 (dreadnoughts, steam). Evidence: first dreadnoughts just commissioned; largely pre-dreadnought fleet

fortification.note: Anchor: 7 (concrete forts). Evidence: Sere de Rivieres fortress belt reinforced in concrete (Verdun, Toul, Epinal, Belfort)

logistics.note: Anchor: 7 (railways). Evidence: dense rail network; Joffre shifted armies by rail before the Marne; Paris taxis

communications.note: Anchor: 7 (telegraph, telephone). Evidence: telephone and telegraph, radio intercepts of German traffic at the Marne

isr.note: Anchor: ISR 7 = aerial reconnaissance. Evidence: aircraft spotted von Kluck's turn east before the Marne

air.note: Anchor: air 7 = 1914. Evidence: leading aero-engine industry (Gnome, Renault)

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (OWID CSV): France 1913 = 5,555, 1914 = 5,158 (2011 int$). August snapshot near the prewar level. B&H Table 1: 3,485 in 1990 int$.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Mid read from Broadberry and Harrison Table 5; low recalled from Ferguson, not read from a fetched source. Low: ~3.9% of NNP in 1913 (Ferguson table 6). Mid: B&H Table 5 government spending 22.3% of GDP in 1914 (10.0% in 1913), less civil spending. High: 46.4% in 1915.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Doughty, Pyrrhic Victory (isbn:0-674-01880-X), not read from a fetched source. Industry ~35% of output in 1913 with ~40% of the labour force still in agriculture (Hautcoeur in Broadberry and Harrison 2005, ch. 6).

foodSurplus.note: Formula: foodSurplus = 1 - agricultural share of employment. Herrendorf, Rogerson and Valentinyi data via OWID: France agriculture share of employment 1906 = 42.7%, 1911 = 41.0%, 1921 = 41.5%. 1 - 0.41 = 0.59 (mid). Near self-sufficient in food before 1914.

annualCohort.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Doughty, Pyrrhic Victory (isbn:0-674-01880-X), not read from a fetched source. ~850,000 births per year in the 1890s, half male, ~75% survival to 20 gives ~320,000; the stagnant population was the motive for the 1913 three-year law.

aircraft_fighter.note: Educated guess. French aircraft output recalled as ~4,500 (1915), ~7,500 (1916), ~14,900 (1917), ~24,600 (1918) from Morrow, The Great War in the Air (not fetched); fighter share (Nieuport, SPAD) a split by judgement.

aircraft_strike.note: Educated guess. Reconnaissance and bomber share of the totals recalled from Morrow (see fighters).

artillery.note: Educated guess. Field and heavy guns per year 1915-1918; 75 mm output reached several hundred per month by 1916.

armor.note: Tanks per year once in production: cited page records 1,000 Renault FT ordered in April 1917; ~3,000 FT built in 1918. No tanks in 1914 (low 0).

ships_major.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. Bretagne class completed 1915-16; capital-ship building stopped in 1914.

ships_minor.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. Destroyers and sloops per year 1915-1918.

submarines.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Conway's All the World's Fighting Ships 1906-1921 (isbn:0-85177-245-5), not read from a fetched source. Submarines completed per year 1915-1918.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Routes nationales and departmentales plus chemins vicinaux; France had the densest metalled road network of the powers.

railKm.note: CHAT railline France: 1913 = 40,770 km (mid), 1914 = 37,400 km (low; appears to exclude lines in the occupied departments). Local lines not included.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Halpern, A Naval History of World War I (isbn:1-55750-352-4), not read from a fetched source. Marseille, Toulon, Brest, Cherbourg, Le Havre, Rouen, Bordeaux, Saint-Nazaire, Dunkirk, Calais, Boulogne.

merchantTonnage.note: Lloyd's Register returns 1914: France 2,201,164 GRT of steam and sail vessels of 100 tons and over (Register Book 1913-14). Converted to deadweight at x1.5 (low x1.3 of the low GRT, high x1.6 of the high GRT).

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Recalled from van Creveld, Supplying War (isbn:0-521-21730-X), not read from a fetched source. van Creveld ch. 4: rail-fed armies operating close to their own network.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Recalled from Doughty, Pyrrhic Victory (isbn:0-674-01880-X), not read from a fetched source. ~3.2M horses in 1913; ~730,000 requisitioned in August 1914.

homeDefense.note: 1.2 row: familiar terrain, fortress belt (Verdun-Toul-Epinal-Belfort), population support.

notes: Snapshot date August 1914 after mobilisation (ordered 1 Aug). Metropolitan France only; North and West African colonial troops (~600,000 raised over the war) and colonial populations excluded, includes empty. Forces are the whole French army; ~1.65M in 62 infantry divisions faced Germany in the north-east. Aircraft all in aircraft_strike (no fighters in 1914). Ship convention: battleships and cruisers = ships_major, destroyers = ships_minor. Book figures (Doughty, Conway's, Morrow) not fetched online, graded at most B.
